title: Amazon kills Alexa’s ability to control Echo speakers' AUX input
gist: Amazon disabled Alexa voice control of the AUX input on older Echo speakers without giving a reason, a small but recurring example of the company removing features from purchased devices while prioritizing subscription Alexa+.

insights.claim: Amazon has disabled voice commands such as 'Alexa, play from line in' for controlling the AUX input on older Echo speakers, affecting the Echo Plus 2nd Gen, Echo 3rd Gen, Echo Studio 1st Gen and Echo 4th Gen.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Illustrates post-sale feature removal on hardware.

insights.claim: Physical AUX inputs, the Alexa app toggle and Bluetooth connections still work, and Amazon says very few people use voice control of AUX, implying few users are affected.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Limited user impact makes this a low-materiality event, but Amazon's materiality claim is unquantified.

insights.claim: Amazon did not answer why it removed the capability or how many users are affected.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Lack of disclosure fuels consumer trust concerns.

insights.claim: Dropping the feature may make Alexa easier for Amazon to maintain as it puts more resources into its AI-powered, subscription-based Alexa+.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Legacy-feature pruning suggests Amazon is reallocating engineering effort toward monetized AI assistant tiers.

insights.claim: Last year Amazon removed users' ability to block Echo devices from sending voice recordings to Amazon on the Echo 4th Gen, Echo Show 15 and Echo Show 10, establishing a pattern of removing functionality from purchased devices.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Repeated removals raise regulatory and reputational risk around connected-device ownership.

insights.claim: Some users view the removal as enshittification, noting it was not a security issue.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Consumer sentiment signal on smart-home platform trust.
insights.quote: I cannot understand the reason they’d simply remove a function beyond enshittification
